recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Do not revert the FHIR-42824 clarification when reviewing this older issue; if FHIR-42824 itself is reconciled in a run that includes Resolved - change required issues, handle it separately under its own key.
issue_request: FHIR-14299 was a Published FHIR-core/FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It asked for CapabilityStatement instances of kind=requirements to import or nest other requirements CapabilityStatements, while clarifying that CapabilityStatement.instantiates asserts conformance to referenced statements and does not import or inherit their content. The approved resolution added a non-normative 0..* canonical(CapabilityStatement) import/imports element and a usage note about non-overlap.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 9ead3299c845b2925dd9482fbf9d43cd7b5136fe / SVN revision 14005, which tightened the CapabilityStatement.instantiates definition and added CapabilityStatement.imports to the then-authoritative CapabilityStatement spreadsheet. Current source has since been refactored to source/capabilitystatement/structuredefinition-CapabilityStatement.xml.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has an active [resources] entry for capabilitystatement=CapabilityStatement, putting the current StructureDefinition source in build scope. Later related issue FHIR-42824 and FHIR-I minutes clarified that sibling imported CapabilityStatements cannot overlap, while the importing CapabilityStatement may refine imported content. The combined branch already contains the FHIR-42824 source clarification.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change was made because the combined branch already has CapabilityStatement.instantiates limited to implemented CapabilityStatements, CapabilityStatement.imports as 0..* canonical(CapabilityStatement), the automatic-instantiates note, and the later sibling-import overlap clarification.
